claims.claim_text: The indexed French lieutenant Christian DeSorbier is a high-confidence match to Christian de Sorbier de Pougnadoresse in the French Sussex-network archive.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Dossier individuel de Christian DE SORBIER DE POUGNADORESSE
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The French official inventory records the uncommon expanded name in a wartime Sussex-network file, and its cross-referenced Resistance list identifies the same adult Christian.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare name, French nationality note, wartime chronology and linked official French archival files; the OSS personnel file has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The archival file spans wartime and postwar administrative dates. It does not establish a pre-OSS employer or the date he joined OSS.
claims.match_notes: Do not merge with the younger Christian de Sorbier born in 1944. The Sussex-network connection is not labeled immediate pre-OSS employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed lieutenant-colonel René Despax is a high-confidence match to French air officer René Louis Auguste Despax, known as Louis Despax in the career register.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The French Resistance inventory links René Despax to GR 16 P 180207; that list expands him to René Louis Auguste, and an Air Force career register lists Louis Despax with the same birth date and lieutenant-colonel rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from three official cross-linked French archive entries plus the indexed rare name and exact rank; the OSS box has not been opened.
claims.temporal_assessment: The inventories establish wartime Resistance-file coverage and a career rank, but not a date-bounded pre-OSS Air Force assignment.
claims.match_notes: The distinct René Jules Despax has a different birth date and a captain/infantry register entry and is not merged into this index person.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gabriel H Desplaines is confirmed as the Army entrant recorded with the spaced surname DES PLAINES.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A unique protected identifier matches, and the first name and middle initial agree despite surname spacing.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by protected identifier and concordant name fields.
claims.temporal_assessment: Army entry was 17 November 1942; OSS entry date is unknown.
claims.match_notes: DES PLAINES is a source spelling/spacing variant, not a separate person.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry in November 1942, Gabriel H Desplaines was classified as a general office clerk.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The protected-identifier-confirmed Army record carries occupation code 105, which the NARA code list defines as general-office clerks.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by unique protected identifier; surname spacing differs but given name and initial match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Date-bounded at Army entry in November 1942; no immediate pre-OSS relationship is established.
claims.match_notes: No firm or agency is named; excluded from employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Jean P Desroberts is a high-confidence match to an Army entry with the same protected identifier and a damaged but concordant name.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The unique private identifier matches the Army record, where the surname is split DES ROBERTS and the given name appears damaged as J AN P.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a unique protected identifier, surname and middle initial; the damaged given name merits archival review.
claims.temporal_assessment: Army entry was 7 February 1942; OSS entry date is unknown.
claims.match_notes: The indexed Jean spelling is preserved; J AN is not silently normalized into Jean in the Army citation.

claims.temporal_assessment: Date-bounded at Army entry in February 1942, not shown to be the immediate pre-OSS occupation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Raymond Deston is a high-confidence match to Lieutenant Raymond Deston of the U.S. Naval Reserve, who led OSS's Central Information Division in 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lieut. Raymond Deston, USNR; Chief, Central Information Division
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A signed 30 April 1945 OSS memorandum carries the uncommon exact name, Naval Reserve rank and division role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from uncommon exact name in a contemporaneous OSS primary document, though the indexed row has no rank or service identifier to independently link the file.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorandum proves service in April 1945, not prewar employment.
